description: Release/drift-tooling registry for Event.kind values that are not part of the current v1 wire contract. Current parsers consume the active event-kind registry and reject these values as schema_violation/unknown_kind; conformance scanners may consume this file for negative drift tests and release audit. This is CI/release drift-detection tooling, not a current-wire normative contract: every entry is hard-reject on the wire, there is no migration/compat tolerance window and no offline migration layer; removed ids MAY appear only in changelog documentation and in cotest negative drift fixtures that assert rejection.

rejection_levels.hard_reject: MUST be rejected at parse/reducer time. No legitimate occurrence on current wire or in current code.
rejection_levels.docs_only: Removed from wire / code; references survive only in CHANGELOG, glossary deprecation notices, or migration guides.

parser_tier_definitions.current_parser: Sync service, federation peer, snapshot consumer, reducer, conformance test runner — anything that processes live or persisted v1 wire bytes. MUST treat every entry in this file as forbidden in input; MUST NOT do payload-shape disambiguation; reject with the schema's standard unknown_kind / unknown_field / schema_violation error.

allowed_context_definitions.changelog: May be referenced in spec or downstream CHANGELOG entries documenting the removal.
allowed_context_definitions.negative_test: May appear in negative fixtures / cotest drift tests that assert hard_reject.

entries.notes: Field-level position move was subsumed by track-relative ordering and per-cell ordered_log lattice; no direct replacement.
Bulk field reordering was removed together with cx.field.position.move; ordering authority lives in track / cell lattice.

Track no longer carries independent membership; access semantics derive from the Strand's effective scope. Use cx.member.state at the Realm boundary, or cx.circle.member.state when Strand.scope_circle_id points at an intra-Realm Circle (see zh/models/circle.md). See current-model 'Track 不携带独立 access'.

History visibility lives on the Realm or Circle boundary, not on a track. Use Realm-level history visibility, or Circle-level when Strand.scope_circle_id points at an intra-Realm Circle (see zh/models/circle.md).

Track-scoped read-receipt override is explicitly out of v1 scope (see discovery/read-receipts.md). Read receipts evaluate at the Strand's effective scope: Realm-default or the Circle referenced by Strand.scope_circle_id.
Track-scoped policy components were removed; policy attaches to the Realm boundary, or to an intra-Realm Circle when Strand.scope_circle_id points at one (see zh/models/circle.md).
Lifecycle snapshot event was decomposed into the canonical create / update / upgrade / archive event kinds plus state events; do not re-introduce a single 'set' kind.
Policy snapshot event was decomposed into per-component policy cells (join-policy, history-visibility, delivery-binding-policy, etc.); do not re-introduce a single 'set' kind.

Disambiguation entry (reject-shape definition). The literal wire Event.kind cx.space.create remains an ACTIVE container-shape event. Current parsers (sync, federation, snapshot, reducer, conformance) MUST NOT inspect payload shape and MUST treat any cx.space.create carrying Realm-level fields (security_class / join_rule / history_visibility / policy_server / delivery_binding_policy) as a schema_violation; they MUST NOT reject the current cx.space.create solely by kind string. This entry only documents the reject shape for current parsers and cotest negative fixtures.
